name: Myeloid effector immunity with neutrophil degranulation and hypersensitivity
rationale: Members are myeloid effector responses (complement receptor signaling, degranulation, ADCC, acute antigen-driven inflammation); hypersensitivity and ADCC separate it from monocyte/SIRP and Fc-inhibitory neighbours, degranulation from the endopeptidase neighbour.

qualifier: phosphoinositide cascades and Klotho co-receptor binding
name: FGFR phosphoinositide cascades and Klotho-dependent ligand binding
rationale: Members are FGF receptor (mostly FGFR4/FGFR1) PI3K, PLC-gamma, FRS/SHC cascades and Klotho-assisted ligand binding; PI3K/PLC phosphoinositide branches and Klotho distinguish it from neighbours built on isoform-specific ligand binding and mutant receptors.

name: Axon regeneration, myelination and glial injury responses
rationale: Members cover axon sprouting/regeneration plus CNS/PNS myelin formation, oligodendrocyte and astrocyte responses; the myelin and glial component separates it from collateral-sprouting/Sema3A neighbours, and the axon regeneration component from the myelination-only neighbour.

qualifier: Rab/ARF GTPase control and postsynaptic receptor trafficking
name: Rab/ARF-regulated endosomal recycling of surface and postsynaptic receptors
rationale: Members concern endosomal recycling and surface localization of receptors including postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptors, governed by Rab/ARF GTPase regulators, which the AMPA-trafficking and presynaptic neighbours lack.

name: CSF1 and DAP12 signaling in macrophage and microglial activation
rationale: Members are M-CSF/CSF1 and DAP12 signaling driving macrophage and microglial proliferation, migration, fusion and cytotoxicity; CSF1/microglia distinguish it from osteoclast, GM-CSF differentiation and negative-glial neighbours.

core: Secretory-pathway maturation of developmental signaling proteins
name: Notch O-glycosylation and Hedgehog autoprocessing and lipidation
rationale: Members are ER/Golgi O-fucosylation/glucosylation of Notch and TSR proteins plus Hedgehog autoprocessing, palmitoylation and release; this pairing separates it from N-glycan, heparan sulfate, palmitoylation-only and somitogenesis neighbours.

name: Perinatal lung alveolar maturation and surfactant homeostasis
rationale: Members cover pneumocyte and saccule development, surfactant metabolism and its genetic defects, and perinatal adaptations (ductus closure, hyperoxia); surfactant distinguishes it from branching-morphogenesis neighbours and alveolar development from gas-transport and scrambling neighbours.

name: Inflammasome assembly, pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 maturation
rationale: Members are canonical and non-canonical inflammasomes (NLRP1/3, AIM2, IPAF, CASP4/5), pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 processing; neighbours are TLR/NOD signaling, IL-17/IL-36 and chemokine production without inflammasome machinery.

name: Plasma cobalamin transport and intracellular cobalamin processing defects
rationale: Members are cobalamin metabolism and inherited defects in TCN2/CD320 transport and MMACHC/MMADHC/ABCD4 processing; neighbours instead cover dietary intestinal uptake or downstream methylmalonyl/propionyl-CoA defects.

qualifier: metanephric comma- and S-shaped body stages
name: Metanephric nephron morphogenesis through comma- and S-shaped bodies
rationale: Members are nephron development and the comma-shaped, S-shaped body and tubule morphogenesis stages; neighbours cover earlier mesenchyme, renal vesicle, ureteric bud and nephric duct events.

name: V-ATPase acidification of lysosomes, endosomes and phagosomes
rationale: Members concern V-ATPase assembly and proton-driven acidification of lysosomal, endosomal, Golgi and phagosomal lumens; phagosome acidification and phagolysosome fusion distinguish it from ion-exchanger, pigmentation and scramblase neighbours.

core: Metabolic regulation by p53 and mTORC1
name: p53 and mTORC1 control of NADPH and central carbon metabolism
rationale: Members link p53, mTORC1 and NRF2 programs to glycolysis, pentose phosphate, isocitrate and NADPH regeneration; NADPH/isocitrate (including 2-hydroxyglutarate) distinguishes it from hypoxia/HIF and broad NFE2L2 neighbours.

name: Purine nucleobase salvage and ribonucleoside catabolism
rationale: Members are PRPP synthesis, HPRT/APRT salvage, ADA/PNP catabolism of inosine/AMP/IMP to allantoin; ribo-salvage separates it from deoxypurine and de novo purine synthesis neighbours.

name: Type II sodium-phosphate cotransport and phosphate homeostasis
rationale: Members are SLC34 Na+/Pi cotransport, its disease variants, PTH and phosphate responses; SLC34 transporters distinguish it from mineralization and anion-exchanger neighbours.

name: ER and mitochondrial stress responses with AKT-FOXO survival control
rationale: Members are UPR branches (ATF6, IRE1/XBP1, PERK/ATF4), eIF2 kinase stress responses, UPRmt and AKT-regulated FOXO transcription deciding survival or apoptosis; FOXO separates it from ER folding/chaperone neighbours and UPR from NFE2L2 neighbours.

name: RAGE and p38-driven monocyte and macrophage recruitment
rationale: Members promote monocyte/macrophage chemotaxis, extravasation and MCP-1 production via RAGE and p38 signaling; positive RAGE/p38-driven recruitment distinguishes it from negative-regulation, neutrophil and monocyte-identity neighbours.

name: Xenobiotic, drug and bilirubin biotransformation and transport
rationale: Members cover phase I/II drug and toxin metabolism (CYPs, FMOs, UGT, sulfation, methylation), drug ADME, organic anion/cation transport and heme/bilirubin clearance; neighbours are bile acid, organic-anion-only and sulfur/selenium metabolism.

name: Neutrophil and monocyte activation with SIRP-mediated phagocytosis restraint
rationale: Members are myeloid activation, degranulation, complement and TLR signaling, with SIRP interactions and negative regulation of phagocytosis/neutrophil activation; the SIRP restraint separates it from formyl-peptide/respiratory-burst neighbours and lack of hypersensitivity/Fc members from others.

name: Axon regeneration and collateral sprouting control
rationale: Members regulate injured-axon sprouting, regeneration and collateral sprouting with RhoA, CRMP and ceramide signaling; collateral sprouting separates it from myelin/glia neighbours and regeneration from Sema3A repulsion neighbours.

name: Gene-specific mRNA translational control by microRNAs
rationale: Members each describe translational regulation of a single transcript (CDH1, CDH11, NPAS4, PD-L1) largely by microRNAs; neighbours cover miRNA biogenesis, general silencing machinery and mRNA decay.

name: Retroviral integration, viral latency and host silencing of retroelements
rationale: Members cover HIV entry, reverse transcription and integration, HCMV events, latency and host HUSH/KRAB-ZFP/ChAHP silencing of viral and endogenous retroelement transcription; the silencing and latency members distinguish it from APOBEC editing and RNA-virus neighbours.

name: Meiotic prophase I recombination and synapsis
rationale: Members are meiotic double-strand break formation and repair, synaptonemal complex, telomere attachment and recombination resolution; neighbours concern meiotic cohesion, chiasma, segregation and female meiosis.

name: Rho GTPase regulation of cytokinesis
rationale: Members are the Rho GTPase cycle and positive regulation of cytokinesis; Rho GTPase control distinguishes it from spindle checkpoint and abscission/contractile ring neighbours.

core: Genotoxic stress response and liver regeneration
name: Genotoxic stress responses and liver regeneration
rationale: Members combine UV, cisplatin, bleomycin and phorbol ester responses with hepatocyte proliferation, differentiation and liver regeneration; the liver component separates it from senescence, light-response and oxidative-stress neighbours.

core: Fc receptor and SIRP immunoreceptor signaling
qualifier: inhibitory restraint of phagocytes and B cells
name: Inhibitory and activating Fc receptor and SIRP signaling
rationale: Members are Fc receptor stimulatory/inhibitory signaling, SIRP interactions and negative regulation of phagocytosis, neutrophil activation and BCR signaling; these immunoreceptor regulators distinguish it from FCGR-ADCC/hypersensitivity and degranulation neighbours.
